doc.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Family's busy creative lives and financial cushion
summary: His wife, daughters and he are all busy with creative work; a union pension, Social Security and royalties on thirty albums keep him afloat.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Yeah. Well Laurence I want to thank you for your time and I admire how busy you have remained and your Tea Time with Laurence Juber, and the success.

Yeah, but you know our whole family, I mean Hope, my wife Hope is, other than working with me on the musical that we’re developing, she’s involved in production of a potential TV show. My eldest daughter, Nico, has written a musical, which she did a Zoom reading of last week with a bunch of really high level New York talent. And then my youngest, Ilsey, has become a very successful songwriter. And she is busy writing and hasn’t stopped, you know, learned how to run Pro Tools so she can record vocals at home. Everybody in the family is just really busy. So happily we’re in a position where we have that flexibility. I mean having — me having done studio work for as long as I have, you know I get a pension from the Musicians Union, and Social Security, and then

I’ve got a revenue stream from royalties on thirty albums that I’ve recorded, you know stuff that gets played on Sirius and Pandora, Spotify, and it all kind of keeps things afloat without having the pressure of having to deal with the fact that there’s no money gigs. So, but I miss the live experience obviously.
